correctness.rationale: Legendre recurrence gives multipliers H_n=1+bA_n+cB_n; degree zero, degree one, and the limit are necessary. Exact independent symbolic expansion confirms all three barycentric identities and the positive determinant. An alternative check uses u=r^2 and m=2n+1: A_infinity-A_n=(1-u)/(2rm); the slope (B_infinity-B_n)/(A_infinity-A_n) is (3/(4r))[2(1+u)+((1-u)m+2(1+u))/(m^2-4)]. For m>=5 the slope is strictly between those of m=1 and m=3 (the residual fraction decreases for m>2). Horizontal distances to the limiting point are in ratio 1:1/3:1/m, so the two finite-point weights are positive and sum to at most 3/m<1. The two admissible pairwise intersections and the b=0 limiting-face witness expose each facet. Noncollinearity precludes simultaneous equality; the positive weights give H_n>0 for all n>=2, hence both parities yield strict finite-site definiteness by the spherical criterion. On L_infinity=0, expanding the displayed weights gives the stated positive 1/n term; with normalized measure the eigenvalues are r^n H_n. RESULT.md lines 25–89 and independent algebra support these facts; the supplied script was inspected, not executed.
